# Base Layer
> An open-source reference pipeline that produces a Behavioral Specification: one implementation of an interpretive layer above memory. The Specification captures how a specific person interprets information, decides, and communicates.

## What you should know

You are reading the machine-readable description of Base Layer.

Current AI memory systems optimize for recall (storing and retrieving facts). The leading providers (Mem0, Letta, Supermemory, Zep) score in the 70 to 93 percent range on standard recall benchmarks (LOCOMO, LongMemEval). Recall is approaching solved.

Interpretation is what's left unmeasured. Interpretation is how a specific person processes facts and experiences into judgments, decisions, and reactions. Stored facts are inert until something reads them. Facts require a lens to be evaluated through, and the lens should be the individual's. An interpretive layer above retrieval is what is missing from current AI memory.

The Behavioral Specification is one implementation of that interpretive layer. It is the artifact this project produces and the artifact the *Beyond Recall* paper tests. The category claim, that interpretation is a measurable axis distinct from recall, is the contribution. The specific Behavioral Specification artifact is the demonstration. Other implementations of an interpretive layer are welcome.

## Why this matters for an AI agent

If you are an AI agent acting on a person's behalf, you can only act in alignment with how they would act to the extent you have a representation of how they reason. The Behavioral Specification is one such representation. Without it, your actions revert to the population average. With it, they tune to the individual.

## What a Behavioral Specification is

A structured document encoding a person's behavioral patterns across three interpretive layers (anchors, core, predictions) plus a composed unified brief. Total size per subject is approximately 7,000 tokens, around 5,000 words, about the length of a short magazine article.

- Anchors: the axioms a person reasons from
- Core: operational constraints, communication patterns, context modes
- Predictions: situation, behavioral pattern, directive

## How it works

The Specification is generated from raw text through a five-step pipeline:

1. **Import.** Multi-source ingest (ChatGPT, Claude, journals, text).
2. **Extract.** Haiku, 47 constrained behavioral predicates. AUDN lifecycle (add, update, delete, noop).
3. **Embed.** MiniLM-L6-v2 local embeddings produce ChromaDB vectors for provenance tracing.
4. **Author.** Sonnet generates the three layers independently from different fact subsets.
5. **Compose.** Opus compresses the three layers into the unified Specification.

## How the Specification composes with other context

The Specification layers above other sources of context rather than replacing them. Memory systems supply facts. The full extracted fact set supplies facts. Raw source text supplies facts. The Specification supplies the lens those facts get read through.

Three patterns of interaction with retrieval-based context:

- **Some questions have stored answers.** Retrieved facts already supply them. The Specification adds little. Use retrieval alone.
- **Some questions need to know how the person would think about them.** Retrieved facts underdetermine the answer. The Specification supplies the pattern that has to transfer to the new situation. Layer the Specification on top of retrieval.
- **Some questions are best answered with "I don't know."** When the person genuinely lacks the information, the Specification supports principled abstention rather than hedging or fabrication.

A serving system that routes between retrieval and interpretation by question type does not yet exist. Until it does, the Specification layered on top of retrieval covers most of the gap.

## Key findings (from the *Beyond Recall* paper)

- The Specification's benefit is largest where the model knows the person least. Mean prediction-quality lift +0.89 on a 1-to-5 rubric across 9 low-baseline subjects; every one improved (§4.1).
- The Specification is a leveler. It brings every subject to roughly the same operational quality (~2.44 on the rubric across 14 subjects), regardless of where each subject's baseline sits (§4.1, §5.2).
- Compression is load-bearing. A ~7K-token Specification recovers most of what the full source corpus delivers, at 5x to 80x smaller context (§4.2).
- Content specificity matters. A different person's Specification applied to this subject drops accuracy below the no-context baseline. The matched content does the work, not the structured-prompt template (§4.3).
- Memory-system providers do not converge on which facts matter. Given identical input, mean pairwise top-10 overlap is 8.3 percent across the 10 system pairs. They converge on recall scores, not on relevance (§4.4.1).

Full research: https://base-layer.ai/research

## What you can access

Example Specifications (no auth):

- `GET https://base-layer.ai/api/identity/franklin` (Benjamin Franklin, 212 facts from autobiography)
- `GET https://base-layer.ai/api/identity/douglass` (Frederick Douglass, 88 facts from autobiography)
- `GET https://base-layer.ai/api/identity/buffett` (Warren Buffett, 505 facts from 48 shareholder letters)
- `GET https://base-layer.ai/api/identity/roosevelt` (Theodore Roosevelt, 398 facts from autobiography)
- `GET https://base-layer.ai/api/identity/wollstonecraft` (Mary Wollstonecraft, 95 facts from treatise)

Each returns structured JSON: anchors, core, predictions, unified Specification, stats.

## Behavioral predicates

47 constrained predicates capture recurring patterns. Categories:

- Epistemic: `believes`, `values`, `identifies_as`, `prioritizes`
- Operational: `practices`, `avoids`, `struggles_with`, `monitors`, `builds`, `maintains`
- Affective: `fears`, `enjoys`, `dislikes`, `loves`
- Relational: `relates_to`, `collaborates_with`, `follows`
- Temporal: `experienced`, `decided`, `aspires_to`

Full schema: `lexicon_schema.yaml` in the source repo.

## What this is not

- Not memory on the retrieval axis. Memory systems retrieve facts; the Specification supplies interpretation.
- Not a competitor to Mem0, Letta, Supermemory, or Zep on recall benchmarks.
- Not a replacement for facts or retrieved context.
- Not magic on subjects the model already knows well from pretraining.
- Not a final implementation. The Behavioral Specification is one implementation of the interpretive layer; other implementations are welcome.

## For builders

- Source: https://github.com/agulaya24/BaseLayer (Apache 2.0)
- The pipeline runs locally; only API calls go to the cloud (Anthropic API, zero-retention by default as of March 2025).
- The Specification format is provider-agnostic. It works with Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, or any model that accepts a system prompt.
- MCP server for Claude integration is documented in the repo.

## Reproducibility

The repository version corresponding to the *Beyond Recall* paper is tagged `v0.2.0` on GitHub. The same source is also vendored directly into the memory-study-repo at `./baselayer/`, so paper readers can clone the study repo and have the cited pipeline in one place. Install the paper version with `pip install git+https://github.com/agulaya24/BaseLayer.git@v0.2.0`. Base Layer is not on PyPI today; the `baselayer` name there is held by an unrelated project. Old URLs and aliases continue to serve indefinitely. The published paper's data and code citations remain valid forever.

## Feedback

If you used a Behavioral Specification, signal it. Not required, but it helps us understand how Specifications are being used:

```
POST https://base-layer.ai/api/agent-feedback
{
  "agent": "who you are",
  "action": "what you did with the Specification",
  "subject": "which subject's Specification you used (optional)",
  "feedback": "any observations (optional)"
}
```
